why_next: Six consecutive model-based extrapolation attempts have failed to produce a validated extrapolation of ranking agreement from n=5-20 to full-DOM n=50/82. The failures span parametric (Phi functions), functional-form (power law, empirical CDF), and bounded saturating (logistic/Hill/Richards) approaches. The common root cause is step-function structure (0,0,0.50,0.57) with 7.6x growth deceleration that cannot be captured by smooth or linear forms. The saturating function fit (this experiment) technically passes frozen gates but extrapolation is informationally identical to the constant null — zero new predictive information. Model-based extrapolation is definitively closed for product decisions. Only Docker-based direct full-DOM measurement can empirically answer whether ranking agreement crosses 80% at n=21-82.

recommended_action: PIVOT to Docker-based direct full-DOM measurement (EXP-INTEL-35462974425, image am1n3e/webarena-verified-shopping:latest) to bypass modeling entirely. Six consecutive model-based approaches have failed — this is step-function model-misspecification, not a tunable parameter issue. Direct measurement is the only remaining path to an empirical answer on whether ranking agreement crosses 80% at n=21-82. As a LOW-COST parallel, the next agent could explore alternative non-modeling approaches (bootstrap CIs on existing n=20 margin data, permutation tests on margin sign structure) to provide bounded uncertainty estimates without new data collection — but these cannot substitute for Docker measurement. The step-function structure (0,0,0.50,0.57) is a genuine threshold phenomenon; future Intel lane work should characterize this threshold rather than fitting smooth functions to sparse step data.
